original_statement: The doubled-arrow construction probably does not give the desired counterexample to base-change stability.
disposition: Proved for HOT and all-derivator strengthened gluing
two_complete_version: The specified fork preserves the HOT condition. For every Der1-4 derivator, Wlc is a fundamental localizer; its cosieve-gluing step follows in the accessible sublocalizer generated by the inclusion.
one_complete_version: The all-derivator W1 gluing step follows from B.5 Loc6a. This concerns the specified fork, not all base changes of the original weak condition.

original_statement: Every universally cohomological D-fibration preserves all constant-coefficient D-equivalences under pullback.
two_complete_version: Input Wlc to a universal weak fibration yields a WD output, not automatically Wlc. A HOT C2-gerbe pulls back a Wlc point-to-S2 equivalence to a non-Wlc fibre inclusion.
one_complete_version: Input W1 yields WD. If all local-system direct images are controlled and Wcoh=W1 (enhanced case), both input and output can be W1.

original_statement: Every universally homological D-fibration preserves all constant-coefficient D-equivalences under pullback.
two_complete_version: Same Wlc failure and dual left-Kan repair; universal hypotheses include all base changes.
one_complete_version: Dual of the preceding W1 repair, using homological comparisons.

original_statement: The implication (b)⇒(a) nevertheless holds for all derivators D_i of i-truncated homotopy types.
two_complete_version: False for sets before replacement by the regular cover EG→BG; still false for Wlc-only restricted fibration repair by the finite gerbe.
one_complete_version: After replacing the comma tests by W1 and using the enhanced equality with cohomological equivalences, universal W1 preservation holds; this is a stronger definition.

original_statement: Universal cohomological/homological D-fibrations as subsequently redefined are closed under composition.
two_complete_version: The rational weak composition example and the finite set-valued 2-complete composition example are verified.
one_complete_version: The complete cohomological class composes. In the enhanced setting it is the W1 version; universal W1 preservation is formally composable.

original_statement: For a universal D-equivalence f:X→Y, restriction f^*:D(Y)→D(X) is fully faithful.
two_complete_version: Every universal WD equivalence is fully faithful on the whole D(B); universal Wlc is sufficient by inclusion.
one_complete_version: Universal W1 is also sufficient by inclusion. All small comma/factorization/disjoint-union shapes are required.

original_statement: For D-fibrations over S, a D-equivalence of total categories must be a D-equivalence on each fibre.
disposition: Refuted for blanket substitutions; model-fibration repair Known
two_complete_version: Finite C2-gerbe H→K has Wlc-equivalent totals over a completely set-aspherical base, but fibre BC2→e is not Wlc. Accessible Wlc Thomason model fibrations restore the assertion.
one_complete_version: Even universal W1-preserving fibrations need not have total-to-fibre detection: reversed transport BC2→e with its section. For HOT structural fibrations, W1 detection does hold under enhancement.

original_statement: The converse of Proposition6(a) holds whenever S is D-contractible.
two_complete_version: The gerbe base K has the homotopy type of S2 and is completely Set-aspherical, so complete base asphericity alone does not repair the Wlc assertion.
one_complete_version: The reversed-transport example has base [1], already contractible; complete base asphericity does not repair this W1 fibration interpretation either.

original_statement: A bundle over the circle is determined up to unique isomorphism by a specified monodromy automorphism of its fibre.
two_complete_version: Automorphisms of a trivial two-sheet bundle remain; replace unique isomorphism by an isomorphism class with the chosen framing/conjugacy convention.
one_complete_version: Independent of coefficient class.

original_statement: Conditions(a)–(c) alone imply that the inclusion of a fibre of(E×Z)/G→E/G is not a D-equivalence.
two_complete_version: E=G discrete regular and reflected circle Z satisfy the stated hypotheses but total quotient is Z and the fibre inclusion is the identity, hence in Wlc.
one_complete_version: Identity counterexample also rules out asserted failure of W1.

original_statement: If additionally H*(Z;k)^G=k, then X=(E×Z)/G is D(k)-aspherical.
two_complete_version: The E=G example works even with completely aspherical base. The manuscript S2/S1 specialization has residual rational H3, verified in a finite categorical model.
one_complete_version: Failure of WD already precludes W1 and Wlc; changing their names cannot remove the missing tensor cross term.

original_statement: The orbit of the six-object poset has the displayed globular relations p1^-p0^-=p1^-p0^+ and p1^+p0^-=p1^+p0^+.
two_complete_version: Correct orbit relations are p1- p0- = p1+ p0+ and p1- p0+ = p1+ p0-.
one_complete_version: Composition-law error independent of localizer; all four sign products checked.

original_statement: Under Der3a′, the revised weakly-contractible-base test condition is equivalent to each of the universal one-sided fibration conditions.
two_complete_version: Der3 a-prime makes local systems constant on weakly contractible test bases; exact fibre/base-change argument proves the weak-condition equivalence. B.3 supplies relative categorical descent, while the composition counterexamples still prohibit the blanket Wlc substitution.
one_complete_version: Enhanced W1 identifies with cohomological equivalence and uses the all-local-coefficients version.

original_statement: If f is Hot-proper then both X_y→X/y and X/y→X/y′ are Hot-equivalences, universally.
two_complete_version: The proper cosieve {1}→[1] has empty and terminal comma categories; the transition is not Wlc.
one_complete_version: The transition is not W1 either. Properness must be supplemented by a transport condition.

original_statement: Footnote55: for HOT, cohomological equivalence, homological equivalence, and constant-coefficient equivalence coincide.
two_complete_version: For HOT all classes equal W-infinity; replacing equivalence by Wlc leaves the statement true.
one_complete_version: Same for W1; mapping-space Yoneda and Cisinski Corollary3.8.

original_statement: Every Hot-equivalence induces an equivalence on locally constant HOT coefficients and hence preserves their cohomology and homology.
two_complete_version: Cisinski Corollary3.8 proves local-system equivalence for every derivator under a nerve weak equivalence.
one_complete_version: Full faithfulness and both local (co)homology comparisons follow by adjunction.

original_statement: For HOT all five equivalence notions coincide with nerve weak equivalence.
two_complete_version: All five HOT equivalence notions equal W-infinity.
one_complete_version: Same.

original_statement: For HOT, D-fibrations do preserve D-equivalences by pullback.
two_complete_version: HOT restricted, universal weak, and universal W-infinity-preserving fibration notions coincide.
one_complete_version: No difference because all HOT equivalence classes agree.

original_statement: With compatible internal Homs, every unqualified D-equivalence is 1-complete.
two_complete_version: Internal Homs do not make a constant equivalence full. e→BC2 over Q and trivial/sign representations give the failure. A Wlc hypothesis implies fullness tautologically.
one_complete_version: Restore adjective cohomological; compatible locally constant internal Homs then prove full faithfulness. Use the monoidal unit, not a stable terminal zero.

original_statement: HOT satisfies c″ and its equivalences are precisely nerve weak equivalences.
two_complete_version: HOT satisfies c-double-prime: W_HOT=W-infinity=W_HOT-lc.
one_complete_version: Same.

original_statement: There should be a single intrinsic HOT-fibration notion on all small categories; the homotopy derivator must be constructed to justify the coefficient route.
two_complete_version: Chapter XI intrinsic HOT-fibrations are universal W-infinity-preserving sharp maps. They need not be the Thomason model fibrations.
one_complete_version: The unique reasonable language is interpreted as the specific equivalences of definitions, not uniqueness among every possible fibration class.
